newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Optimism about South Africa's economic prospects gained momentum on Wednesday as the rand pierced the key 4.50 level to the dollar and the South African Chamber of Business confidence index reached its highest level since October.
- Government has moved to contain its mounting debt resulting from providing forward cover, by telling electricity utility Eskim it will no longer subsidise cover for long-term borrowings.

- The Medicines Control Council had prohibited further research on controversial AIDS drug Virodene until serious issues regarding the drug's safety and study design had been resolved, council chairman Prof Peter Folb said on Wednesday.

- The cabinet on Wednesday endorsed Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's debt and cash management measures, including a plan to do away with possible conflicts of interest between the finance ministry and the Reserve Bank in the financial markets.

- Anglo American Corporation of SA Ltd is co-operating with a British mining and exploration company to develop a Namibian zinc deposit, which could result in construction of a 500 million rand mine and smelter by 200.

- The government is turning to foreign investors to help accelerate housing delivery and meet the goal of building a million houses within five years, Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele, the housing minister, said on Wednesday.
- Cabinet has approved measures to separate the market-making role of the Reserve Bank from its regulatory functions, Trevor Manuel, the finance minister, said on Wednesday.
- Masterfridge, the local fridge manufacturer, has exceeded market expectations with a steep 67 percent increase in earnings to 16.56 cents a share in the six months to December 31.
- Widespread scepticism about the AIDS drug Virodene has deepened following a ban on further research and testing imposed by the Medicines Control Council on Wednesday.
